title: Authorization Forensics Orchestration Guide
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This guide defines the cross-functional orchestration process for deriving, preserving, and packaging authorization and authentication evidence during security incidents. It ties RBAC decision traces, continuous audit-logging, data-residency constraints, SDLC gate artifacts, and compliance packaging into a single operational flow. The target audience is Security Engineers, SREs, Platform, and Legal/Compliance.
body_2:
Goals:
- Ensure evidence is preserved in a forensically sound manner within stated retention / residency constraints.
- Provide reproducible queries and tooling to collect entitlement and access telemetry within 2 hours of incident detection.
- Define decision ownership and SLAs for evidence handoff to Legal and Compliance.
- Maintain auditability for model-serving related access (API keys, model variant swaps, and admin tooling).
body_3:
Scope:
This document covers: RBAC decision logs, authn/authz telemetry, application and infra audit streams, object storage & key material custody metadata, SDLC gating artifacts for deployments that may influence incidents, cross-border constraints on evidence movement, and packaging steps for regulatory review (e.g., SOC2, ISO27001, GDPR). It does NOT replace the incident response runbook for containment and eradication; it augments the evidence retention and chain-of-custody procedures.
body_4:
Ownership and Roles:
- Incident Commander (IC): Security Incident lead. Primary contact for evidence requests. SLA: acknowledge evidence request within 30 minutes.
- Forensics Lead: Senior Security Engineer responsible for evidence integrity and packaging.
- Platform/SRE: Provide access to cluster-level audit streams and retained artifacts.
- Identity & Access Owner: RBAC system owner who can interpret entitlement data (IAM/SCIM/OKTA).
- Legal/Compliance: Request and receive evidence packages; adjudicate residency requests and provide legal holds.
- Data Custodian: Owner of the data stores (S3/GS/Blob) where logs and artifacts are preserved.
- Product/Model Owner: Point of contact for model serving changes that might relate to the incident.
body_5:
Key Definitions:
- Authz Event: Any allow/deny decision emitted by the authorization service (format defined in Audit Event Schema below).
- Access Trace: End-to-end idempotent identifier that ties a client request through the proxy, ingress, model server, and datastore. Usually a UUID in header X-Redwood-Trace.
- Evidence Bundle: A compressed, signed archive (.tar.gz + detached signature) containing logs, hashes, and a manifest describing provenance and residency constraints.
- Short-term retention: 90 days (fast-access index). Long-term retention: per customer / legal hold rules; default 3 years for privileged sessions evidence.
body_6:
Audit Event Schema (canonical example):
- Event (JSON newline-delimited):
  {
    "timestamp": "2026-01-18T14:23:12Z",
    "trace_id": "53f2b6e4-1a7b-4d2c-9a2f-6f8b2eaf1c3d",
    "service": "proxy-ingress",
    "principal": { "type": "service_account", "id": "svc-model-deployer" },
    "action": "model.deploy",
    "resource": { "type": "model", "id": "redwood://models/gptx-8b@v3" },
    "decision": "allow",
    "policy_id": "policy-az-42",
    "residency": "us-west-2",
    "evidence_ref": "s3://redwood-audit/us-west-2/2026/01/18/53f2b6e4.log"
  }
- Field rules:
  - timestamp: RFC3339 UTC
  - trace_id: UUID v4, present on all ingressed requests
  - principal.id: stable service or user id (do not embed PII)
  - residency: the physical region / legal region tag.
  - evidence_ref: canonical pointer into the immutable audit store.
- Storage: events are ingested into the audit-edge (Kafka topic id: audit.events.prod) and then sharded to region-specific immutable stores with object lifecycle policies.
body_7:
Evidence Preservation SLA and Routing:
- Detection window: when an incident is triaged as requiring authorization evidence, the Forensics Lead issues an Evidence Preservation order.
- SLA: evidence collection start within 60 minutes; initial package delivered to Legal/Compliance within 8 hours (for high-severity incidents).
- Residency-aware routing: If the incident involves EU customer data or a request from an EU principal, raw artifacts must remain within eu-west-1 unless Legal permits export. Requests to copy artifacts out require a documented data export approval.
- Immutability: use the immutable-audit-store (WORM) feature for all preserved artifacts. Hashes (SHA-256) must be computed and recorded in the manifest for every file.
body_8:
Collection and Packaging Steps (checklist):
1) Record Scope: IC and Forensics Lead define search scope (trace IDs, time window, affected principals, model IDs).
2) Quarantine Streams: Lock relevant partitions in Kafka topics (audit.events.prod, authz.decisions, admin.activity) to prevent retention-based deletion.
3) Snapshot Artifacts:
   - cluster state (kubectl get pods -o yaml) for affected namespaces
   - IAM change logs and SCIM provisioning deltas (last 7 days)
   - Proxy and model-server logs filtered by trace_id
   - Storage object manifests (preserve referenced S3 keys)
4) Assemble Bundle:
   - create manifest.json with provenance fields (collector, start_ts, end_ts, hash list)
   - compress: tar -czf evidence-<incident>-<ts>.tar.gz <artifacts>
   - sign: gpg --detach-sign evidence-<incident>.tar.gz
5) Register Bundle in Evidence Registry: POST to /internal/evidence with metadata and hash. Registry returns an evidence_id and qa checklist.
6) Handoff: For Legal/Compliance provide evidence_id, manifest, and residency constraints. If foreign transfer is required, include Data Export Approval ticket id.
body_9:
Sample CLI snippets:
- Query events by trace: redwood-auditctl query --trace 53f2b6e4 --start 2026-01-18T14:00:00Z --end 2026-01-18T15:00:00Z --out /tmp/trace-events.json
- Lock Kafka partition: kafkactl lock --topic audit.events.prod --partition 12 --reason "IR-2026-0134 evidence preservation"
- Assemble manifest example (manifest.json):
  {
    "incident": "IR-2026-0134",
    "collected_by": "a.patel@redwood.ai",
    "start_ts": "2026-01-18T14:00:00Z",
    "end_ts": "2026-01-18T15:30:00Z",
    "files": [ { "path": "proxy-53f2.log", "sha256": "a3b5..." } ]
  }
body_10:
Chain-of-Custody Manifest Fields (required):
- evidence_id, collector, collection_start, collection_end, prior_storage_uri, current_storage_uri, sha256, signed_by, signature_pubkey_id, residency_label, legal_hold_id (optional).
body_11:
SDLC and Deployment Artifacts to Include:
- CI job logs for deployment (job id, git sha, pipeline run time).
- Rollout controller snapshots (canary config, traffic weights).
- Model artifact hashes and quantization profiles.
- Approval records: who allowed the rollout (identity, statement), especially for emergency/override flows.
- Feature flags toggles at incident time.
body_12:
Risk & Exception Handling:
- Low-level entitlement noise: define filtering heuristics to avoid over-collection (e.g., service-to-service heartbeats).
- Legal holds override retention policies: when Legal issues a hold, lifecycle policies must be suspended for the affected keys and replication must preserve residency constraints.
- Exception approval flow: Technical exception requests (e.g., to export EU artifacts for deep-dive) require:
  1. Security justification (documented),
  2. Legal sign-off,
  3. Expiration and revocation time,
  4. Evidence of secure transfer (SFTP with key exchange or customer-approved transfer method).
body_13:
Observability and SLOs for Evidence Processes:
- Evidence collection latency SLO: P50 < 25 minutes, P95 < 75 minutes for critical incidents.
- Manifest generation accuracy: 99.9% of bundles must pass automated manifest/hash checks.
- Audit ingestion latency: events must appear in audit.events.prod stream within 60s of generation 99% of the time.
- Alerting: missing trace_id correlation or failures during GPG signing surface as P1 to Security PagerDuty.
body_14:
Compliance Packaging Matrix (quick reference):
- SOC2: include manifest, system configuration, change approvals, authz decision logs (90 days minimum).
- ISO27001: include chain-of-custody proofs, signed bundle, and KMS key rotation evidence.
- GDPR/Data Subject Requests: minimal export of data only with Legal approval; anonymize principal identifiers when possible.
- Local regulator (examples): APAC regulators may require retention in-region; map residency_label -> required_region in the registry.
body_15:
Post-Incident Actions:
1) Audit completeness review: Forensics Lead runs the manifest validator and uploads a summary to the incident timeline.
2) Retention tuning: SRE/Platform adjusts retention windows (if allowed) to prevent future loss.
3) Policy updates: If the incident revealed gaps in the audit schema, update schema and roll out a migration plan.
4) Lessons learned and evidence handling drills: Schedule a tabletop within 10 business days with Legal, Security, and SRE.
body_16:
Appendix A: Evidence Registry API (examples)
- Register bundle: curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/v1/evidence \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <svc-token>' \n  -F 'manifest=@manifest.json' \n  -F 'bundle=@evidence-IR-2026-0134.tar.gz'
- Query evidence metadata: curl https://internal-api.redwood/v1/evidence/<evidence_id> -H 'Authorization: Bearer <svc-token>'
body_17:
Appendix B: Quick mapping table for evidence residency
| residency_label | allowed_regions | export_policy |
| us | us-west-2, us-east-1 | internal-only unless Legal approves |
| eu | eu-west-1, eu-central-1 | must remain in eu unless Data Export Approval |
| apac | ap-southeast-1 | region-local with supervisor approval |
